title.narrative: Validating Khaloom’s recycled textile production in Bangalore, India

description.narrative: India is the largest textile producer in the world and employs over 4.3 million hand workers, of which over 80% is female. Recent studies show that 57% of textile workers live in poverty and face poor working conditions and unemployment rates are increasing due to automation in the industry. Due to the use of chemicals and water current recycling practices have a negative impact on the environment. The demand for high quality recycled cotton is growing globally as clothing manufacturers feel pressure to make their production processes and supply chain more sustainable. Khaloom, a spin-off of Enviu and Sympany, recycles post textile production cotton waste into yarns and textiles and aims to contribute to zero waste production chains and meet the increased demand for recycled textiles. In order to prepare for further scale-up and investments in India, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to develop and validate a local production model by the set-up of a scalable production facility, the employment and training of female weavers, the development a product range that meet industry requirements and the development of a branding strategy to prepare for further expansion of the production facility and future orders. The project directly supported 20 jobs, mostly female, supported 3 local designers and provided training to 25 weavers on how to produce recycled textiles. Furthermore, the project contributed to better working conditions of the employees by offering equipment and a safe working environment. In addition, the company offers its employees’ health insurance and at least 1.5 times higher wages than industry average and with this strongly improves the livelihood and liveable income of its employees, in particular that of its female employees. The project has been successful and further investments are currently being explored which may result in the direct support of an additional 75 jobs.
